reason: ALIGNED is evaluated with either an MLP or a KB-embedded GNN as its neural component.
The brain encoder EEGProject is linear layers, frozen CLIP vision branches are used, and the method is also run with ShallowNet/DeepNet/EEGNet/TSconv brain encoders.
The GFlowNet policy is parameterized as a graph transformer with MLP output heads.
Experiments train a two-layer MLP on MNIST for fidelity and Pythia-410M and GPT2-Small language models at scale.
CM2 uses ResNet34, LSTM and TinyBERT encoders with an LSTM fusion module, plus Gaussian mixture marginals and a copula fitted by variational inference.
TStruct is described only as parameterized shared temporal dependency matrices with generated combination weights; no model family is named.
The motion encoder uses residual convolutional blocks and Transformers, the classifier is a BiGRU, and frozen vision encoders include CLIP and Qwen3.5.
AbNovo is a score-based diffusion model whose network combines an ESM2-initialized 33-layer Transformer protein language model, Evoformer trunks and Invariant Point Attention.
PPL encodes and decodes keypoints with MLP-Mixer blocks around a learnable memory; no other family is named.
The only model family named as trained by the authors is the Decomp_v3 AutoEncoder evaluator fine-tuned on ELMA; baseline families are not described.
Fast-SAM3D modifies the inference of SAM3D's diffusion generators and token-based decoders (step caching, token carving and aggregation).
The annotation pipeline uses stable diffusion/ControlNet colorization and fine-tunes SAM with LoRA; no CNN is named.
The curation uses a convolutional autoencoder plus K-means, and benchmarks train CNNs (ResNet, EfficientNet, custom CNN) and transformers (ViT, DeiT, Swin).
Diff3R fine-tunes the DPT Gaussian head of Depth Anything v3 and adds a small MLP to predict the regularizer; no CNN is used.
Experiments use ResNet-50 and MobileNet-v2, ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/16, and an MLP-Mixer-Nano trained from scratch.
The target tertiary structure is encoded with a GVP-GNN within the MARL policy.
Hybrid models combine neural ODEs with convolutional encoders/decoders and feed-forward networks.
CORAL trains an AlphaFold3-style Pairformer-Diffusion model, fine-tunes DrugFlow, and screens training poses with a prompted GPT-5 agent.
The rigging fine-tunes RoBERTa classifiers on responses generated by querying the target LLMs.
Screener learns dense SSL descriptors with a Gaussian density model and is distilled into a UNet; normalizing flows are only a comparison point.
